question: Which two primary afferent fibre types are responsible for conducting nociceptive signals from peripheral tissues to the dorsal horn?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Aα fibres are large, myelinated fibres that conduct proprioception and motor signals. Aβ fibres transmit touch and pressure — not nociception primarily.
Correct. Aδ fibres (thin, myelinated) mediate fast, sharp 'first pain'; C fibres (unmyelinated) mediate slow, burning 'second pain' — together they form the nociceptive afferent limb.
Aβ fibres primarily conduct light touch. Under central sensitisation conditions they can contribute to allodynia, but they are not primary nociceptors.
Aβ fibres carry mechanoreceptive signals. Pairing Aδ with C fibres is the correct nociceptive pair.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review nociceptor afferent fibre classification: Aδ (myelinated, fast) and C fibres (unmyelinated, slow) are the primary nociceptive conductors.
Well done. Knowing Aδ (fast, sharp) vs C (slow, burning) fibre properties is foundational to understanding pain pharmacology and spinal cord mechanisms.
